database_summary: Sakila-like DVD rental schema (SQLite). Contains actors, films, customers, stores, staff, inventory, rentals and payments plus geographic lookup tables (country, city, address), classification tables (language, category) and many-to-many bridges (film_actor, film_category). Mix of mostly current-state descriptive tables and event/history tables (rental, payment).

accepted.name: film_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  rental_rate,
  length,
  replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
accepted.description: Normalized film master rows with key descriptive attributes and canonical numeric measures. Useful as the base film dimension for joins, filtering, and aggregations (e.g., revenue by film, film counts by rating/category). | Use for: List films with attributes; join to categories/actors/inventory; Filter films by rating, language, release_year, or length; Use rental_rate or replacement_cost in aggregations

accepted.name: film_category_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id,
  f.title,
  f.release_year,
  f.language_id,
  f.rental_rate,
  f.length,
  fc.category_id,
  c.name AS name,
  fc.last_update AS last_update
FROM film_category fc
JOIN film f ON fc.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
accepted.description: Denormalized mapping of films to their categories with film descriptive columns. Useful for category-level aggregations, counts, or filtering films by category name. | Use for: Count films per category or list films in a category; Aggregate revenue or rentals by category after joining payments/rentals/inventory; Filter films by category name and other film attributes

accepted.name: film_actor_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.film_id,
  fa.actor_id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  f.title,
  f.release_year,
  fa.last_update
FROM film_actor fa
JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
JOIN film f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
accepted.description: Mapping of films to actors with actor name columns and film identifying info. Useful for actor filmographies, counting films per actor, or filtering films by actor. | Use for: List films for a given actor or actors for a given film; Count films per actor or co-actor networks; Filter films by actor attributes combined with film attributes

accepted.name: inventory_by_film_store
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  store_id,
  COUNT(inventory_id) AS inventory_count
FROM inventory
GROUP BY film_id, store_id
accepted.description: Inventory counts per film and store (one row per film_id, store_id) with available inventory measure. Useful to join to rentals/payments to compute utilization or to see stock distribution across stores. | Use for: Compute availability or stock per film per store; Join inventory counts to rentals to compute turnover or utilization rates

accepted.name: rental_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.rental_id,
  r.rental_date,
  r.return_date,
  r.inventory_id,
  inv.film_id,
  inv.store_id,
  r.customer_id,
  r.staff_id,
  r.last_update
FROM rental r
LEFT JOIN inventory inv ON r.inventory_id = inv.inventory_id
accepted.description: Event-level rentals enriched with customer, inventory, film and store identifiers and rental timing. Useful for time-based analyses, lifetime metrics, and joining to payments. | Use for: Calculate rental durations, on-time returns, or active rentals over time; Join rentals to payments or customers for revenue and retention analyses

accepted.name: payment_by_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS payment_total,
  MIN(payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
  MAX(payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment amounts and counts per customer (one row per customer) for customer-level revenue analysis and LTV-style metrics. | Use for: Compute revenue per customer, frequency, and recency; Segment customers by payment_total or activity

accepted.name: customer_contact
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.store_id,
  c.first_name,
  c.last_name,
  c.email,
  c.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  ct.city,
  ct.country_id,
  co.country,
  a.postal_code,
  a.phone,
  c.active,
  c.create_date,
  c.last_update
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN address a ON c.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ct ON a.city_id = ct.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ct.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Customer rows with address, city and country descriptive columns for geographic segmentation and contact-level attributes. | Use for: Geographic distribution of customers, mailing lists, or contact-based filters; Join customers to payments/rentals to compute regional metrics

accepted.name: customer_ltv_features
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  COALESCE(p.payment_count,0) AS payment_count,
  COALESCE(p.payment_total,0.0) AS payment_total,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(p.payment_count,0)>0 THEN (p.payment_total / p.payment_count) ELSE 0.0 END AS avg_payment,
  COALESCE(r.rental_count,0) AS rental_count,
  COALESCE(r.first_rental_date, NULL) AS first_rental_date,
  COALESCE(r.last_rental_date, NULL) AS last_rental_date
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count, SUM(amount) AS payment_total
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
) p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(rental_id) AS rental_count, MIN(rental_date) AS first_rental_date, MAX(rental_date) AS last_rental_date
  FROM rental
  GROUP BY customer_id
) r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
accepted.description: Customer-level summarized features combining payments and rentals: counts and totals for payments and rentals along with average payment amount. Useful for churn/LTV modeling and segmentation. | Use for: Build features for customer lifetime value or churn models; Segment customers by engagement or revenue metrics

accepted.name: store_staff_manager
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.store_id,
  s.manager_staff_id,
  s.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  ct.city,
  ct.country_id,
  co.country,
  s.last_update
FROM store s
LEFT JOIN address a ON s.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ct ON a.city_id = ct.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ct.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Store-level rows with manager staff info and address for store-level reporting and geographic joins. | Use for: Report sales or rentals by store location; Associate store manager or store geography with performance

accepted.name: film_rental_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.film_id,
  COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count,
  MIN(r.rental_date) AS first_rental_date,
  MAX(r.rental_date) AS last_rental_date
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory inv ON r.inventory_id = inv.inventory_id
GROUP BY inv.film_id
accepted.description: Counts of rentals per film (aggregated from rental->inventory->film) with first/last rental dates. Useful for popularity metrics and trend analyses. | Use for: Rank films by number of rentals or measure popularity; Combine with inventory to compute turnover

accepted.name: ranked_films_by_rentals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.film_id,
  fr.rental_count,
  fr.first_rental_date,
  fr.last_rental_date,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY fr.rental_count DESC) AS rentals_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    inv.film_id,
    COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count,
    MIN(r.rental_date) AS first_rental_date,
    MAX(r.rental_date) AS last_rental_date
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory inv ON r.inventory_id = inv.inventory_id
  GROUP BY inv.film_id
) fr
accepted.description: Films ranked by rental_count with a dense rank. Exposes a rank column so downstream queries can select top-K films by rentals without embedding ranking logic. | Use for: Select top-N most rented films by filtering rentals_rank <= N; Compare ranks across time by reusing ranking CTE with time filters
